title: Normalized completed-coefficient direct image on strict diagrams
statement: Let l be prime and E a finite extension of Q_l. For any scheme morphism f:X to Y and a supplied completed structural map c satisfying all finite projection equations and the constant-to-completed compatibility square, and supplied SiteData source,target [def-pur-completed-pushforward-models], there exists DiagramComparisonData D l E f with D.source=source, D.target=target and D.structureMap=c. Its completed structural map is fixed by the finite projections; its constant, finite and quotient squares have identity underlying section maps and the universal-unit normalizations. The quotient unit and composition equations, the strict-system square, the tower evaluation squares and the direct-image/inverse-limit comparison hold with all the stated representative and projection normalizations. No completeness or reconstruction conclusion is part of this assertion.

proof.text: Obtain the coefficient-only comparison C, retaining the supplied source, target and structural map.

Use the Grothendieck structure of module towers to choose a normalized total derived levelwise pushforward T. Construct evaluation squares with identity ordinary comparison by the generic derived coefficient-comparison helper, since tower evaluation preserves K-injectives. Invert the supplied exact factor isomorphisms to put its unit equation in Square.normalization form.
Extend C and the now fixed tower image T to the strict-system square, retaining its evaluation section identities.

Direct image preserves ordinary tower limits, detected after forgetting to abelian presheaves. Use preservesLimitNatIso, whose components are limit.post. The target derived-limit unit is invertible on pushed K-injective towers by the acyclicity lemma. The generic normalized derived-composition helper gives limitComparison and limitNormalization for the supplied images and limits.

Prove limitProjection by rightDerived_ext for the composite of source inverse limit and completed pushforward. Cancel the source evaluation factor, use limitNormalization, naturality of the target projection, and normalization of the evaluation square. The two limitProjection_normalization equations reduce the equality to limit.post followed by a projection equals pushforward of that projection; the evaluation ordinary map is identity by its section identity. Assemble the full DiagramComparisonData and retain the three supplied-model equalities.

lean.statement:
theorem directImageDiagrams_exists {X Y : Scheme.{t}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (source : SiteData l E X) (target : SiteData l E Y)
    (c : R l E Y ⟶ (ringPush.{t, u} f).obj (R l E X))
    (hc : ∀ n, c ≫ (ringPush.{t, u} f).map (projection l E X n) =
      projection l E Y n ≫ finiteStructure l E f n)
    (hconstant : integralConstantToCompletionOfUniverses l E Y ≫ c =
      constantStructure l E f ≫
        (ringPush.{t, u} f).map (integralConstantToCompletionOfUniverses l E X)) :
    ∃ D : DiagramComparisonData l E f,
      D.source = source ∧ D.target = target ∧ D.structureMap = c
